en: To avoid someone or something; or to stay at a distance from them.
ex: Keep away from the fire; it's dangerous.
離火遠一點，很危險。

en: To leave a place; or to explode; or (of an alarm) to start ringing; or (of food) to become bad.
ex: The alarm went off at six sharp.
鬧鐘在六點整響起。

en: To say something loudly; or to ask for someone's help or attention by shouting.
ex: She called out to him across the street.
她隔著街對他大喊。

en: To continue to communicate with someone.
ex: We promised to keep in touch after graduation.
我們約定畢業後保持聯絡。

en: To go with someone to say goodbye; or to send something somewhere.
ex: We went to the station to send him off.
我們到車站為他送行。

en: To contact someone, especially by phone or email.
col: get in touch with an old friend
ex: I'll get in touch with you next week.
我下週會跟你聯絡。

en: To wait for a short time; or to keep holding something; or to keep going in a difficult situation.
ex: Hold on while I check the schedule.
請稍等，我查一下時間表。

en: To remove clothing; or (of a plane) to leave the ground; or to suddenly become successful; or to leave work.
ex: The plane took off on time.
飛機準時起飛。

en: To interrupt someone while they are speaking.
ex: She cut him short before he could finish.
他還沒說完就被她打斷了。

en: To agree to something that you did not want to agree to; or to allow other vehicles to go first.
ex: Drivers must give way to pedestrians.
駕駛人必須禮讓行人。

en: To begin a journey toward a place.
ex: We start for Tokyo tomorrow morning.
我們明天早上動身去東京。

en: To want very much to do something.
ex: I'm dying to hear the news.
我迫不及待想聽到這個消息。

en: To appear similar to someone or something; or to seem likely to be something.
ex: He looks just like his brother.
他長得很像他哥哥。

en: To have a good opinion of someone or something; or to agree with something.
ex: My parents don't approve of my choice.
我父母不贊成我的選擇。

en: To understand something; or to receive or obtain something; or to be punished.
ex: Oh, now I get it.
喔，我現在懂了。

en: To pretend that something is true, especially in a game.
col: make believe to be a doctor
ex: The kids made believe they were astronauts.
孩子們假裝自己是太空人。

en: To defend yourself against someone or something unfair or powerful.
ex: The people stood up against the dictator.
人民起而反抗獨裁者。

en: To form an opinion after considering all the facts.
ex: What conclusion can we draw from this?
我們能從這裡得出什麼結論？

en: To seem about to happen, especially something unpleasant; or to be present as a threat.
ex: The threat of war hung over the country.
戰爭的威脅籠罩著這個國家。

en: To keep a distance from someone or something.
ex: Please stand away from the platform edge.
請遠離月臺邊緣。

en: To fail to keep up with others; or to not pay money you owe on time.
ex: He fell behind because he was sick.
他因為生病而落後了。

en: To save something for later use; or to stop thinking about something for the moment.
ex: She puts aside a little money each month.
她每個月都存一點錢。

en: To return something to a place; or to say that you did not mean what you said.
ex: I take back what I said earlier.
我收回我先前說的話。

en: To end a relationship; or to separate into smaller parts; or to stop a meeting.
ex: They broke up after two years.
他們交往兩年後分手了。

en: To be so interested in something that you do not notice other things.
ex: She was lost in thought and didn't hear me.
她陷入沉思，沒有聽見我說話。

en: To stay at a distance and not become involved; or to stop in a dispute without taking action.
ex: The two sides stood off for hours.
雙方僵持了好幾個小時。

en: To be in a situation where you are blamed or punished for doing something wrong.
col: get into trouble with the law
ex: He got into trouble for being late again.
他又因遲到而惹上麻煩。

en: To give something to someone for free; or to reveal a secret accidentally.
ex: The shop is giving away free samples.
這家店正在免費贈送試用品。

en: To not go to bed at your usual time.
ex: We stayed up all night talking.
我們聊了一整夜。

en: To be trapped by something unpleasant such as bad weather or traffic; or to be involved in a situation.
ex: We were caught in the rain without umbrellas.
我們沒帶傘卻遇上了雨。

en: To expect or hope to get something from someone; or to take care of something; or to be careful.
ex: Many people look to him for leadership.
許多人期待他的領導。

en: To begin and seem likely to continue, usually used about something unpleasant.
ex: Winter set in early this year.
今年冬天來得早。

en: To agree with someone's plans or ideas; or to be friendly with a group of people.
ex: They fell in with our plans.
他們同意了我們的計畫。

en: To go past someone or something; or (of time) to go by; or to visit a place briefly.
ex: Years passed by, and nothing changed.
歲月流逝，一切依舊。

en: To continue to follow a plan, rule or belief; or to remain loyal to someone.
ex: Please stick to the topic.
請不要離題。

en: To become less strong or intense; or to gradually disappear.
ex: The wind died down by evening.
傍晚時風勢漸漸減弱。

en: To pretend to be something; or to do something without serious effort.
ex: The children are playing at being pirates.
孩子們在玩扮海盜的遊戲。

en: To lead someone around a place and show them things; or to carry something with you.
ex: She took us around the old city.
她帶我們逛了舊城區。

en: To make someone so excited that they lose self-control; or to remove something by force.
ex: Don't get carried away by the success.
別被成功沖昏了頭。

en: To prevent someone from doing something; or to not tell someone about something.
ex: I couldn't keep from laughing.
我忍不住笑了出來。
